symptom: During mandatory same-operation recovery, the configured runner stopped before checks because its official preflight received the canonical label where the CLI accepts only an unsigned decimal slice input.

evidence.configuredRunnerReceipts: Both sequences produced two RUNNER_RESPONSE_CAPTURED receipts; the model's semantic response was BLOCKED before any verification command because preflight did not return authority.

reproductionCanonicalLabel.diagnostic: EXECUTE_SLICE is not legal from RUNNER_INITIALIZATION_BLOCKED; legal next operation is EXECUTE_SLICE for slice-01

evidence.priorNormalStateEvidence: The same configured runner returned TESTS_PASS and the correct authority in sequence 6 from MATERIALIZED_PRISTINE; the error appears on the recovery path when the runner model constructs the preflight command from the canonical recovery slice label.

rootCause: The shared official preflight API intentionally accepts an unsigned decimal slice argument and normalizes it to slice-NN. The parent driver already converts canonical labels with canonicalSliceInput, but the auxiliary model re-created the preflight command using slice-01 during same-operation recovery. This caused the strict official gate to report no authority before any check could run.
responsibleBoundary: production runner launcher handoff of the already-authorized official preflight result to the configured independent runner
correction: Replace model-generated duplicate preflight invocation with the exact official result computed by the production driver using the existing canonicalSliceInput and preflightExecutionOperation exports. The driver will deliver the result as trusted launcher-owned payload; the runner will compare its operation, slice, SPEC_PATH, and sha256 authority with the request and selected artifacts, then resume at the logical runner invocation when mandatoryRecovery matches. The strict execution runtime remains unchanged.
whyCodeInsteadOfPrompt: The model selected the canonical label required by the runner payload, but the CLI has a different numeric argument representation. This deterministic conversion already exists in the driver; another instruction would leave the LLM responsible for serializing a known mechanical value.

regression.plannedBehavior: A synthetic mandatory-recovery result from the official preflight is supplied byte-exactly to the configured runner without a second model-authored CLI invocation; mismatched operation, slice, SPEC_PATH, authority, or recovery target is rejected before runner start.
regression.runtimeInvariant: The numeric official preflight accepts only the exact legal same-operation recovery; the canonical label remains valid in the workflow payload and runner interface.

liveReplay: Local regressions pass. In fresh Case C sequences 7 and 8, the production-v2 driver supplied numeric inputSlice=1 and the exact mandatory recovery preflight. The runner callback then failed earlier because C128 omitted the separate top-level SPEC_PATH field; no runner receipt was created, so those events do not prove the auxiliary runner consumed C127's trusted preflight.
